passages.text: Then Job answered: “Truly then you are the people with whom wisdom itself will die!
passages.sermon:
Job spoke.
Job answered his friends.
Job said, “You think you are the people who have wisdom.
You believe wisdom will die with you.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ אָ֭מְנָם כִּ֣י אַתֶּם־ עָ֑ם וְ֝עִמָּכֶ֗ם תָּמ֥וּת חָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: But I also have a mind; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job says he has a mind like they do.
Job says he is not less than they are.
Job says everyone knows these things.
passages.original: גַּם־ לִ֤י לֵבָ֨ב׀ כְּֽמוֹכֶ֗ם לֹא־ נֹפֵ֣ל אָנֹכִ֣י מִכֶּ֑ם וְאֶת־ מִי־ אֵ֥ין כְּמוֹ־ אֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: I am a laughingstock to my friends, though I called on God, and He answered. The righteous and upright man is a laughingstock.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks.
Job is a righteous and upright man.
Job called on God.
God answered Job.
Job’s friends laugh at him.
People mock the righteous and upright man.
passages.original: שְׂחֹ֤ק לְרֵעֵ֨הוּ׀ אֶֽהְיֶ֗ה קֹרֵ֣א לֶ֭אֱלוֹהַּ וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑הוּ שְׂ֝ח֗וֹק צַדִּ֥יק תָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: The one at ease scorns misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.
passages.sermon:
A person who lives in comfort feels secure.
This person does not fear trouble.
This person looks down on those who suffer misfortune.
This person thinks misfortune only happens to people who are already falling.
This person scorns those whose lives are unstable.
passages.original: לַפִּ֣יד בּ֭וּז לְעַשְׁתּ֣וּת שַׁאֲנָ֑ן נָ֝כ֗וֹן לְמ֣וֹעֲדֵי רָֽגֶל׃

passages.text: The tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure— those who carry their god in their hands.
passages.sermon:
Robbers live in tents.
Their tents are safe.
People who provoke God feel secure.
They hold their god in their hands.
God allows this to happen.
God gives them this security.
passages.original: יִשְׁלָ֤יוּ אֹֽהָלִ֨ים׀ לְשֹׁ֥דְדִ֗ים וּֽ֭בַטֻּחוֹת לְמַרְגִּ֣יזֵי אֵ֑ל לַאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֵבִ֖יא אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But ask the animals, and they will instruct you; ask the birds of the air, and they will tell you.
passages.sermon:
Animals can teach you.
You can ask them.
Birds live in the sky.
You can ask the birds.
They will tell you.
passages.original: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁאַל־ נָ֣א בְהֵמ֣וֹת וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וְע֥וֹף הַ֝שָּׁמַ֗יִם וְיַגֶּד־ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; let the fish of the sea inform you.
passages.sermon:
The earth can teach you.
You can speak to the earth.
The fish of the sea can tell you things.
The fish will inform you.
passages.original: א֤וֹ שִׂ֣יחַ לָאָ֣רֶץ וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ לְ֝ךָ֗ דְּגֵ֣י הַיָּֽם׃

passages.text: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
passages.sermon:
God made all things.
God acts with power.
Every creature knows this.
No animal, bird, earth, or fish is unaware.
All creation understands that the LORD’s hand did this.
passages.original: מִ֭י לֹא־ יָדַ֣ע בְּכָל־ אֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֥י יַד־ יְ֝הוָה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: The life of every living thing is in His hand, as well as the breath of all mankind.
passages.sermon: God holds the life of every living thing in His hand.\r\nGod holds the breath of all people in His hand.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ֭יָדוֹ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־ חָ֑י וְ֝ר֗וּחַ כָּל־ בְּשַׂר־ אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes its food?
passages.sermon:
The ear tests words.
The tongue tastes food.
The ear examines what it hears.
The tongue judges what it eats.
passages.original: הֲלֹא־ אֹ֭זֶן מִלִּ֣ין תִּבְחָ֑ן וְ֝חֵ֗ךְ אֹ֣כֶל יִטְעַם־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Wisdom is found with the elderly, and understanding comes with long life.
passages.sermon: Elderly people have wisdom.\r\nPeople who live a long time gain understanding.
passages.original: בִּֽישִׁישִׁ֥ים חָכְמָ֑ה וְאֹ֖רֶךְ יָמִ֣ים תְּבוּנָֽה׃

passages.text: Wisdom and strength belong to God; counsel and understanding are His.
passages.sermon:
God possesses wisdom.
God possesses strength.
God owns all counsel.
God owns all understanding.
passages.original: עִ֭מּוֹ חָכְמָ֣ה וּגְבוּרָ֑ה ל֝֗וֹ עֵצָ֥ה וּתְבוּנָֽה׃

passages.text: What He tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man He imprisons cannot be released.
passages.sermon:
God acts with absolute power.
God can destroy something.
No one can rebuild what God destroys.
God can imprison a person.
No one can release the person God imprisons.
passages.original: הֵ֣ן יַ֭הֲרוֹס וְלֹ֣א יִבָּנֶ֑ה יִסְגֹּ֥ר עַל־ אִ֝֗ישׁ וְלֹ֣א יִפָּתֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: If He holds back the waters, they dry up, and if He releases them, they overwhelm the land.
passages.sermon:
God has all wisdom and strength.
God controls the waters.
If God holds back the waters, the waters dry up.
If God releases the waters, the waters flood the land.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן יַעְצֹ֣ר בַּמַּ֣יִם וְיִבָ֑שׁוּ וִֽ֝ישַׁלְּחֵ֗ם וְיַ֖הַפְכוּ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: True wisdom and power belong to Him. The deceived and the deceiver are His.
passages.sermon:
God holds all power.
God possesses true wisdom.
God owns the deceived.
God owns the deceiver.
passages.original: עִ֭מּוֹ עֹ֣ז וְתֽוּשִׁיָּ֑ה ל֝֗וֹ שֹׁגֵ֥ג וּמַשְׁגֶּֽה׃

passages.text: He leads counselors away barefoot and makes fools of judges.
passages.sermon:
God has true wisdom and power.
God controls all people.
God leads counselors away with nothing.
God makes judges act like fools.
passages.original: מוֹלִ֣יךְ יוֹעֲצִ֣ים שׁוֹלָ֑ל וְֽשֹׁפְטִ֥ים יְהוֹלֵֽל׃

passages.text: He loosens the bonds placed by kings and fastens a belt around their waists.
passages.sermon:
God holds all wisdom and power.
God controls kings.
God loosens the bonds that kings place.
God fastens a belt around the waists of kings.
passages.original: מוּסַ֣ר מְלָכִ֣ים פִּתֵּ֑חַ וַיֶּאְסֹ֥ר אֵ֝ז֗וֹר בְּמָתְנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: He leads priests away barefoot and overthrows the established.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and authority.
God leads priests away without shoes.
God removes their honor and status.
God overthrows those who are established and strong.
God brings down people who seem secure.
passages.original: מוֹלִ֣יךְ כֹּהֲנִ֣ים שׁוֹלָ֑ל וְאֵֽתָנִ֣ים יְסַלֵּֽף׃

passages.text: He deprives the trusted of speech and takes away the discernment of elders.
passages.sermon: God acts with power and authority.\r\nGod removes speech from those who are trusted.\r\nGod takes away understanding from elders.
passages.original: מֵסִ֣יר שָׂ֭פָה לְנֶאֱמָנִ֑ים וְטַ֖עַם זְקֵנִ֣ים יִקָּֽח׃

passages.text: He pours out contempt on nobles and disarms the mighty.
passages.sermon: God acts with power and authority.\r\nGod pours out contempt on nobles.\r\nGod disarms the mighty.
passages.original: שׁוֹפֵ֣ךְ בּ֭וּז עַל־ נְדִיבִ֑ים וּמְזִ֖יחַ אֲפִיקִ֣ים רִפָּֽה׃

passages.text: He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadows into light.
passages.sermon:
God reveals hidden things.
These things are deep and covered by darkness.
God brings the deepest shadows into the light.
Nothing remains hidden from God.
passages.original: מְגַלֶּ֣ה עֲ֭מֻקוֹת מִנִּי־ חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וַיֹּצֵ֖א לָא֣וֹר צַלְמָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: He makes nations great and destroys them; He enlarges nations, then disperses them.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power over all nations.
God makes some nations great.
God destroys those same nations.
God enlarges nations.
God then scatters those nations.
passages.original: מַשְׂגִּ֣יא לַ֭גּוֹיִם וַֽיְאַבְּדֵ֑ם שֹׁטֵ֥חַ לַ֝גּוֹיִ֗ם וַיַּנְחֵֽם׃

passages.text: He deprives the earth’s leaders of reason and makes them wander in a trackless wasteland.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power over all people.
God removes wisdom from the leaders of the earth.
God causes these leaders to lose understanding.
God makes them wander in confusion.
They walk in a wasteland with no path.
passages.original: מֵסִ֗יר לֵ֭ב רָאשֵׁ֣י עַם־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם בְּתֹ֣הוּ לֹא־ דָֽרֶךְ׃

passages.text: They grope in the darkness without light; He makes them stagger like drunkards.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power over people.
He causes some people to lose their way.
They move in darkness.
They do not have any light.
They reach out and try to find their path.
They cannot see where to go.
God makes them wander.
They stagger like drunkards.
They cannot walk straight.
They are confused and lost.
passages.original: יְמַֽשְׁשׁוּ־ חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־ א֑וֹר וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם כַּשִּׁכּֽוֹר׃
